title: Boss: the receipt
summary: Four small scripts that use everything from this module.

steps.title: Module boss
steps.body: No new ideas. You have print, f-strings, numbers, strings, input and truthiness. These programs make you combine them. Each reads input, so test with more than one case.

steps.title: Name tag
prompt: Read a first and last name (two lines). Print the last name in capitals, a comma, the first name with only its first letter capitalised.
hints: `str.capitalize()` makes the first letter upper and the rest lower.

steps.title: Time on the clock
prompt: Read a number of seconds. Print it as `H:MM:SS`, with minutes and seconds always two digits. Hours may be any size.
hints: `//` and `%` peel off hours, then minutes.
`:02` pads a number to two digits with zeros.

steps.title: Palindrome check
prompt: Read a line. Ignoring case and spaces, print `yes` if it reads the same backwards, otherwise `no`.
hints: `a if cond else b` is Python's `cond ? a : b`.

steps.title: The receipt
prompt: Read an item name, a unit price in dollars (may have decimals), and a quantity (whole number), on three lines. Print a receipt 24 characters wide:
- Line 1: the name left-aligned in 20 characters, then `x`, then the quantity right-aligned in 3.
- Line 2: `@ `, the unit price with 2 decimals left-aligned in 12, then the total as `$` plus 2 decimals, right-aligned in 10.
Every line is exactly 24 characters, so the numbers line up on the right. If the name line is blank, use `Item`.
> **Tip:** `format(total, '.2f')` is the f-string spec as a function, handy for building `'$' + ...` before aligning the whole thing.
steps.starter:
name = input()
price = float(input())
qty = int(input())
hints: The prompt gives you the exact f-strings; the work is reading and converting the input.
